I'll write the kernel to sum over k in the same sequential order as the CPU version, preserving order even with tiled shared-memory accumulation across tiles.\n\nFor timing, I'll measure the whole GPU compute path including host-to-device copy, kernel execution, and device-to-host copy, since that's the honest end-to-end cost compared to the CPU's pure computation time -- I'll note this difference explicitly. Validation still happens on the CPU using the copied-back result, so that part stays straightforward.\n\nI also need to preserve edge-case behavior: an N=0 input should skip GPU allocation entirely rather than crash on division by zero in validation, and zero-duration runs should just produce an infinite GFLOPS value as before. Since there's no CPU fallback, I'll require a GPU and error out if none is available, while leaving matrix initialization on the host since that isn't the part being parallelized -- using plain std::vector for host memory rather than pinned memory to keep things simple.\n\nI'm adding a CUDA_CHECK macro for error checking with synchronization calls, and setting up CMake to target the RTX 3090 (sm_86) with a reasonably portable list of architectures since minimum CMake version support for CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES varies -- I'll bump cmake_minimum_required to 3.18 and specify an explicit architecture list rather than relying on \"native\". I also need to make sure -march=native only applies to C++ host compilation, not CUDA, using a generator expression to scope it by language.\n\nNow I'm sorting out compiler flags, splitting optimization options so -O3 and -march=native apply correctly for both CXX and CUDA (routing host-only flags through -Xcompiler), and deciding to leave FMA contraction at its default since reproducibility tolerance against CPU results doesn't require disabling it.\n\nFor the kernel itself, I'm designing a tiled shared-memory matmul in double precision using 64x64 block tiles with 4x4 register blocking per thread (16x16 threads, BK=16), keeping summation order preserved. I need to account for boundary conditions when N isn't a multiple of tile size by zero-padding loads and adding bounds checks on stores.\n\nI'm reasoning through whether zero-padded k values could alter sums via -0.0 edge cases, and conclude guarding the inner loop to only iterate over valid k within each tile preserves the exact operation sequence safely.\n\nWriting kernel constants...\n\nChecking memory access patterns, the shared memory reads for As broadcast well within a warp since only two distinct addresses are needed, while Bs reads have moderate bank conflicts across the sixteen tx threads—acceptable tradeoff for keeping the kernel simple.\n\nNow I'm working out the tile loading loops: each of the 256 threads loads four elements into As and Bs with bounds checks against N, then the inner compute loop multiplies corresponding row/column values from shared memory into the accumulator registers, handling the boundary case where the last k-tile is smaller than BK.\n\nFor the store step, I write results back to global memory only when within bounds, and I'm being careful about FMA contraction matching the reference implementation's `sum += A*B` pattern so the results agree bit-for-bit. {"type":"text","timestamp":1792985618431,"sessionID":"ses_e89bb66dfffezcxves2nohHLTP","part":{"id":"prt_176455795001GzKG9owVjx7gMC","messageID":"msg_176455369001tmS6Gh5TtZjVT3","sessionID":"ses_e89bb66dfffezcxves2nohHLTP","type":"text","text":"Next is the CMake change: enable the CUDA language and set the flags so the host-only options don't reach `nvcc`.","time":{"start":1792985618325,"end":1792985618419}}}
{"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1792985620383,"sessionID":"ses_e89bb66dfffezcxves2nohHLTP","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"toolu_01Ah4X2iyKotA4KkhnL8jxcm","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/matmul_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_cuda_r2/matmul/CMakeLists.txt","content":"cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.18)\nproject(matmul_benchmark LANGUAGES CXX CUDA)\n\nset(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)\nset(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)\nset(CMAKE_CUDA_STANDARD 20)\nset(CMAKE_CUDA_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)\n\n# Target GPU architectures (override with -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=...)\nif(NOT DEFINED CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES)\n    set(CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES 75 80 86 89 90)\nendif()\n\n# matmul.cpp contains CUDA kernels, so compile it with nvcc\nset_source_files_properties(matmul.cpp PROPERTIES LANGUAGE CUDA)\n\nadd_executable(matmul matmul.cpp)\n\n# Enable optimizations\ntarget_compile_options(matmul PRIVATE\n    $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CXX>:-O3 -march=native -Wall -Wextra>\n    $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CUDA>:-O3 -Xcompiler=-march=native,-Wall,-Wextra>\n)\n\n# Link math library and CUDA runtime\ntarget_link_libraries(matmul m CUDA::cudart)\n"},"output":"Wrote file successfully.","metadata":{"diagnostics":{},"filepath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/matmul_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_cuda_r2/matmul/CMakeLists.txt","exists":true,"truncated":false},"title":"home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/matmul_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_cuda_r2/matmul/CMakeLists.txt","time":{"start":1792985620296,"end":1792985620340}},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"caller":{"type":"direct"}}},"id":"prt_1764557fb001cu0yJg79ZZM9AF","sessionID":"ses_e89bb66dfffezcxves2nohHLTP","messageID":"msg_176455369001tmS6Gh5TtZjVT3"}}

{"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1792986009734,"sessionID":"ses_e89bb66dfffezcxves2nohHLTP","part":{"id":"prt_1764b3052001x6jNfmyhyIljW1","messageID":"msg_1764b2c6a001ppSyjhwccceo8e","sessionID":"ses_e89bb66dfffezcxves2nohHLTP","type":"reasoning","text":"Since the original binary itself isn't internally consistent about FMA use across loops, I'll just keep the default FMA path for best performance and note that results match within normal floating-point rounding tolerance, which validation confirms is acceptable.\n\nI should also check the N=0 edge case — the original would crash on modulo-by-zero during validation, and my version preserves that same behavior since it's unchanged. Without -v, N=0 just prints an empty result and timing, matching the original's path too. Performance-wise, I'm hitting around 190 GFLOPS at N=2048 on the 3090, well under its ~556 GFLOPS FP64 peak, so there's room to push further with bigger register tiles.\n\nI'm weighing whether to tune the tile sizes further (like 8x8 per-thread tiles with 128x128 blocks) versus just reporting honest numbers — I'll skip heavy tuning since the gains would be marginal relative to effort. Instead, I want to run compute-sanitizer's memcheck on an odd-sized case to catch any memory issues cheaply, then do a final pass confirming the out-of-source CMake build compiles warning-free with -Wall -Wextra, and re-verify timing and -v correctness across several sizes including the default N=512.\n\n","time":{"start":1792986001490,"end":1792986009658},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}
